entities.name: Primary alcohol to aldehyde oxidation
observations: The encoded transformation converts the terminal benzylic/aryl-substituted primary alcohol (–CH2OH) to the corresponding aldehyde (–CHO).
The methoxy ether, sulfur-containing heteroaromatic ring, alkyne, and other unsaturation are unchanged in the encoded net transformation.

entities.name: DMP oxidation
observations: Dess–Martin periodinane in dichloromethane, commonly near room temperature, is a plausible selective primary-alcohol-to-aldehyde oxidation system.
This is a standard proposed reagent system, not a substrate-specific documented condition.

entities.name: Swern oxidation
observations: Swern oxidation uses DMSO and oxalyl chloride followed by triethylamine, typically initiated at low temperature and then warmed, and is plausible for alcohol-to-aldehyde conversion.
This is a standard proposed reagent system, not a substrate-specific documented condition.

entities.name: TPAP NMO oxidation
observations: Catalytic TPAP with NMO, typically in dichloromethane, is a plausible primary-alcohol-to-aldehyde oxidation system.
This is a standard proposed reagent system, not a substrate-specific documented condition.

entities.name: PCC or PDC oxidation
observations: PCC or PDC can oxidize a primary alcohol to an aldehyde under controlled conditions, but conditions should limit overoxidation and possible sulfur-containing heteroaromatic sensitivity.
This is a standard proposed reagent class, not a substrate-specific documented condition.

entities.name: No exact oxidation record
observations: The available reaction search found no directly documented oxidation record for the exact substrate; a fuzzy related record concerned downstream reductive amination of the aldehyde scaffold and does not establish oxidation reagents or yield.
